title: Netflix Celebrates 10 Years of Korean Stories in Seoul
summary:
Stars from "Squid Game" and "KPop Demon Hunters" took the stage in Seoul on October 24 as Netflix celebrated 10 years in Korea with a fan festival. The two-day event, called Netflix Janchi, ran October 24-25 at Sangam Oil Tank Culture Park, where thousands of fans enjoyed themed booths, games, merchandise, and live music.

"Squid Game" was represented by Lee Jung-jae, Lee Byung-hun, and Park Hae-soo, while Ahn Hyo-seop appeared for "KPop Demon Hunters." Other stars included Koo Kyo-hwan and Jung Hae-in of "D.P.," Kim Hyun-joo of "Hellbound," and Yum Hye-ran of "Mask Girl."

"Ten years ago, we dreamed big. But none of us could have imagined that Korean stories would move hearts around the world, and land right at the center of global culture," said Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos. He previewed "Possible Love," Lee Chang-dong's Venice winner, arriving November 6, and "Tantara," starring Song Hye-kyo, Gong Yoo, and Kim Seol-hyun, following on December 11. Still undated are "Grand Galaxy Hotel," "She, Wolf," "All of Us Are Dead" Season 2, and "Solo Leveling."

Netflix launched in Korea on January 6, 2016. Its first international film was Bong Joon Ho's "Okja." The first Korean original, the stand-up special "Yoo Byung Jae: Too Much Information," arrived in March 2018, and "Kingdom" became its first Korean series in January 2019. In July 2021, "Kingdom: Ashin of the North" became the first Korean show to enter the Global Top 10, charting in 58 countries.

Netflix has counted more than 200 Korean titles on its Global Top 10 since June 2021. "Squid Game" Season 1 holds the record for the longest run, at 32 straight weeks, nine at number one. Its three seasons are the streamer's three most-watched non-English series ever, and more than four in five subscribers worldwide have sampled at least one Korean title. "For Netflix, Korea is more than a market. It is where we discovered new possibilities, and where we learned how far a story can travel," Sarandos said.
why_it_matters: Korean stories have grown from one country's shows into some of the world's most-watched series, showing how a story told in one language can travel across the globe.

background_read: Netflix is a streaming service that lets people watch shows and films over the internet, and it makes its own original shows in many countries.
Korean stories are shows and films made in Korea, in the Korean language, which have found fans far beyond Korea.
A fan festival is a public event where fans meet stars, play games, and enjoy themed booths and live music celebrating the shows they love.
The Global Top 10 is Netflix's chart of its most-watched titles around the world, so entering it means a show is being watched in many countries at once.
